cases.packet: Decision: evaluate targeted retrieval and citation/coverage audit, optional specialized roles, and lean repository context against simple baselines. ICML debate abstract cautions against default debate; OpenScholar full article reports specialized scholarly retrieval and synthesis; LiRA abstract reports specialized literature roles; ContextBench and AGENTS.md preprints report context-selection and cost limits. ContextBench concerns issue resolution and AGENTS.md findings distinguish generated and developer context; do not remove required instructions. Cheapest falsifier: compare relevant context used, missed alternatives, errors, reviewer effort and cost on matched tasks; compare optional role splits separately. Unresolved: target transfer, unpublished review status for both preprints and role-split benefit. Rejected SWE-bench abstract as nondiscriminating and generic debate studies as redundant; retain conditional positive debate evidence.

stage_matrix.terra_reason: Independent verifier supports the bounded decision implication; target transfer remains untested.
stage_matrix.caveat: General benchmark debate strategies do not establish useful software architecture critique or model-tier transfer.
stage_matrix.original_claim: Evidence does not justify defaulting to multi-agent debate as the way to discover useful alternatives: in a peer-reviewed benchmark study, debate protocols did not reliably outperform self-consistency or ensembles, though tuning some protocols improved results and made them sensitive to settings.
stage_matrix.original_discriminator: On a small matched set of real repository decisions, compare a scoped evidence brief with and without a single adversarial reviewer; measure expert-discovered useful alternatives, factual support, review time and cost.

stage_matrix.terra_reason: Independent verifier supports the bounded decision implication; target transfer remains untested.
stage_matrix.caveat: OpenScholar is a specialized scholarly retrieval/synthesis system evaluated on literature QA benchmarks; it does not establish that iterations always help or validate repository-scoped claims.
stage_matrix.original_claim: For literature synthesis, retrieval of relevant passages, attribution, iterative retrieval-based verification, and evaluation of citations/coverage/factual correctness are empirically useful components; OpenScholar reports gains for an 8B model and a GPT-4o-backed pipeline on its ScholarQABench tasks.
stage_matrix.original_discriminator: Audit a sample of submitted claims against cited source passages, tracking unsupported/misattributed claims and whether direct links let the architecture decision-maker resolve disagreements quickly.

stage_matrix.terra_reason: Independent verifier supports the bounded decision implication; target transfer remains untested.
stage_matrix.caveat: The abstract's domain is systematic literature-review production, not architecture decisions or heterogeneous model coordination; no cost or patch-acceptance result.
stage_matrix.original_claim: Role-specialized multi-agent workflows have a positive but domain-limited published example: LiRA assigns outlining, subsection-writing, editing and reviewing roles and reports improved writing/citation quality on scientific review datasets.
stage_matrix.original_discriminator: Compare a single broad repository investigation against two bounded, disjoint evidence questions with one expert synthesis; judge novel actionable findings and time to decision.

stage_matrix.terra_reason: Independent verifier supports the bounded decision implication; target transfer remains untested.
stage_matrix.caveat: Preprint status only; evaluates repository issue-resolution context retrieval with frontier models, not architecture-alternative discovery by lower-tier scouts.
stage_matrix.original_claim: Repository exploration should be treated as a retrieval/selection problem with observable quality dimensions: ContextBench evaluates context precision, recall and efficiency and reports a gap between explored and used context, with elaborate scaffolding yielding only marginal retrieval gains in its evaluation.
stage_matrix.original_discriminator: For actual investigations, sample whether cited source locations are decision-relevant and whether any consequential alternative was missed; track retrieval breadth and report size alongside expert utility.

stage_matrix.terra_reason: Independent verifier supports the bounded decision implication; target transfer remains untested.
stage_matrix.caveat: It studies issue-fixing success and cost rather than investigation quality; developer-written and generated context differ, and the result does not justify removing useful local practice instructions.
stage_matrix.original_claim: Repository context files are not a guaranteed shortcut: a recent arXiv study across four agent/model configurations found generated context files did not significantly improve success and increased inference cost over 20% on average; repository overviews were not useful, while instructions for non-standard practices may still be useful.
stage_matrix.original_discriminator: Use a matched local evaluation of current versus proposed research prompt on the same repository questions, scoring supported alternatives, omissions, citation accuracy, review effort and cost.

original_rejected.reason: Useful context that repository-level issue work spans multiple functions/files and is challenging, but it evaluates patch completion, not investigation/prompt workflows; the opened arXiv record exposed only the abstract and did not change the decision implications above.

original_rejected.item: Additional generic debate and multi-agent system studies surfaced in search
original_rejected.reason: Not pursued after the ICML benchmark supplied both negative and conditional-positive evidence directly relevant to whether debate should be the default; extra broad results would be redundant within the operation budget.

original_unresolved: No retrieved study directly tests whether lower-reasoning subagents discover better architecture alternatives in existing repositories under mixed-model coordination. The proposed workflow therefore needs a matched local evaluation.

The sources do not establish that any prompt method preserves prompt-injection resistance, expert access to decisive sources, independent patch acceptance, or timely consequential review; these remain explicit process constraints to retain and separately assess.

ContextBench and AGENTS.md findings are arXiv preprints in the accessed records; publication status may change. LiRA and MAD full papers were not opened, so their reported results are bounded to publisher abstracts and metadata.
